summary: Front and rear range lights of 1900 on the west shore of Margaree Harbour, Cape Breton, guiding ships in from the Gulf; designated heritage lighthouses in 2019.

access.note: LighthouseFriends: grounds and towers closed; the rear light can be viewed from Route 219.

range lights established in place of the breakwater light; catoptric apparatus
converted to battery power; official keepers no longer required

Coast Guard renovation of the rear tower, then the front tower

notes_for_editor: Records and sources. (1) COST, CORRECTED: the 1901 Chief Engineer's report gives $1,062.95 for the Margaree range buildings (printed pp. 60-61, scan p. 75-76), the same figure LighthouseFriends gives. The $814.29 figure that the first draft attributed to Margaree belongs to Charlo harbour, in the same report on printed p. 60 (scan p. 75); the first draft misattributed it. The story now gives $1,062.95 and no longer states a disagreement. (2) Ownership: LighthouseFriends says the Canadian Coast Guard owns the lighthouse (front light page; it describes a planned divestiture, no date). The NS Lighthouse Preservation Society page covers the FRONT light only and says it is 'Owned by the Margaree Harbour Heritage Lighthouse Group'; the first draft wrongly said it listed both lights. The record agency stays CCG with this caveat. (3) Colour: the 1901 report and LighthouseFriends say red (fixed red); the current CCG list says F Y (fixed yellow) for both; NSLPS says 'Fixed Red (1922)'. Left for a human check against a current photograph or the CCG record. (4) Position: the Canadian Register gives the rear light as 65 m in front of the front light in one entry and the front light as 65 m behind the rear in the other; the story says only that the two stand one behind the other. (5) Dates: the Storm King stranding is 'May 5' in the report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1913 (printed p. 187, scan p. 194), so 1913 follows; the Laura wreck is 'spring 1904' in the 1905 report (printed p. 23, scan p. 28). (6) Keepers 1880-1886 are LighthouseFriends' names under the front light; the 1880 men kept beacon lights and the breakwater light, not the 1901 range towers. (7) The 1909 keepers' table (Canadian report, fiscal 1909) matched Miles A. Dunn and R. McLellan to the two Margaree lights by column position in OCR text; it was not used for dates. (8) A 1909 report entry for 'Margaree' (lighthouse tower and keeper's dwelling rebuilt, $1,116.68) is not clearly this station and is not used. (9) The 1901 report's ranges say 'ten miles', not nautical miles; the story uses the current list's nautical-mile ranges only. (10) Newspapers: a Chronicling America search for Margaree Harbour and Storm King for 1912-1914 returned no hits, so no newspaper is cited. (11) LighthouseFriends is a copyrighted secondary source; facts are restated in our own words and quotations are short. (12) PAGES: the 1900 report text is on printed p. 48 (scan p. 63); the 1901 Margaree entries are on printed pp. 60-61 (scan pp. 75-76); the Storm King entry is printed p. 187 (scan p. 194); the storm-signal line is printed p. 165 (scan p. 172); the Electra line is printed p. 39 (scan p. 46). The Laura line is printed p. 23 (scan p. 28), where the OCR index was checked.
